55K likes, 240 comments - realhinakhan on October 3, 2026: "Rule no 1 
Please take ACCLIMATIZATION seriously 🙏🏻
Ladakh is no joke.. 
I have seen perfectly fit people suffer and how..
Proper precautions = Great memories 🙌

Carrying or renting an oxygen backup in Ladakh is a useful safety precaution for remote high-altitude travel, but proper acclimatization remains your primary defense against altitude sickness.

Your daily supplements and Diamox, A prescribed medication (plz consult your physician for dosage modification) It Helps prevent and reduce symptoms of acute mountain sickness by helping the body adjust to high altitudes.

Proper layering is essential to handle Ladakh’s extreme temperature swings between sunny days and freezing nights.

Carrying a pulse oximeter and a digital thermometer is mandatory and potentially life-saving when traveling to Ladakh. Because Ladakh sits at extreme high altitude with  Leh at roughly 11,500 feet.. the atmospheric pressure drops. This drop severely decreases blood oxygen saturation levels (SpO₂), placing travelers at risk for Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) and hypothermia..

Toilet hygiene and cleanliness is a must.. 
Many long highway stretches, mountain passes, and roadside stops have no restrooms or basic facilities.
make sure you carry basic essentials like 
Pocket tissues, hand sanitisers, toilet seat sanitiser, toilet seat covers for road travel in Ladakh..

The high-altitude desert air is very dry, which quickly causes throat irritation and a tickling cough. You can easily buy standard throat-soothing lozenges or herbal options like kanthil or laung at local pharmacies and general stores.
Laung and Kanthi really helped me a lot..

Category 4 sunglasses are the gold standard for high-altitude environments, blocking 92–97% of visible light to prevent from intense UV rays..Solar radiation increases by roughly 10% for every 1,000 meters of elevation hence it can be very damaging, it also protects from snow blindness and severe eye strain.

Neck gaiter 
Thanks to @ashukla09 for introducing me to NECK GAITER.
It will help block the fine dust entering your nose and mouth at High-altitude trails and road travels.. loose dirt and strong winds make your throat extremely dry .. mak".

33K likes, 486 comments - realhinakhan on September 24, 2026: "Some voyages must begin before the day even begins.

So I started before the waking dawn, and reached the arid, Potala-esque Thiksey Monastery just as the first light of the Sun arrived.

The chants, the atmosphere, the stillness of soulful morning prayers, meditation, everything made the journey to find The Self feel easier than I could have imagined.
Meditation heals me 🙏🏻

I have always found moments to connect with the divine, sometimes by looking outward and sometimes by looking within. The world has so much to offer, both outside and inside us.
Today, that quest found a memorable milestone.

Thank you @utladakhtourism for making it so comfortable for us.. 

#thikseymonastery #reelitfeelit #meditation #healingfromwithin #ReelsWithHK".

posts.meta_description:
55K likes, 315 comments - realhinakhan on September 14, 2026: "It was an absolute honour to be invited by the Indian Army to visit the Goodwill Schools, schools for children with special needs, and hospitals run by the Indian Army in Kashmir.

A special and heartfelt Thanks to Lt Gen Pratik Sharma, Army Commander, Northern Command, Brig S K Pradhan, VSM, BGS (IW), Northern Command, 
and Lt Col Akshay Rajput(you are a rockstar), GSO-1 (Media & PR), Northern Command and other officers and soldiers for the warmth, hospitality and for giving me the opportunity to witness this incredible endeavour up close.

I was also deeply honoured to meet some of the brave soldiers who fought in Op Sindoor. Meeting them and hearing about their service was an experience I will carry with me with immense pride.

We often speak about our Armed Forces for the battles they fight and the borders they protect. But seeing their work beyond the battlefield was truly eye-opening. They are not only protecting lives, they are helping build them.

From education and healthcare to employment and creating opportunities for the people of Kashmir, the Indian Army is doing so much to empower communities and help them prosper. What I witnessed was incredibly encouraging, and honestly, I was amazed by the scale and sincerity of these efforts.

What impressed me most was their sheer humility. They do so much without asking for recognition or applause. But I believe their efforts must be seen, spoken about and appreciated. Knowing about the great work they do can only inspire all of us.

There are so many unsung heroes and so many superstars working quietly behind the scenes. I am truly in awe of them and of the work being done for the people of Kashmir.

Our forces are truly heroes on and off the battlefield. 🇮🇳

A special shout out to all the soldiers, teachers, doctors and staff who continue to serve and contribute to the prosperity of the people of Kashmir with such dedication.

I leave these schools and hospitals with immense pride, gratitude and a renewed respect for the men and women who serve our nation.
@indianarmy.adgpi 

Jai Hind. 🇮🇳".
